title: US Air Force Orders Final $2.82B Boeing KC-46A Lot as Dark Eagle Hypersonic Battery Fields, Japan Secures Access to Indian Missile Ranges, and Israel Adds $5B to Defense Budget
subhead: The Pentagon closes out Boeing's original fixed-price tanker contract and confirms full fielding of the Army's first Dark Eagle hypersonic battery, while Tokyo looks to India's test ranges for long-range strike weapons and Turkey's ASELSAN and MKE advance precision air and naval munitions.

sections.heading: US Air Force Awards Boeing $2.82 Billion for Final KC-46A Lot as Army Fields First Dark Eagle Hypersonic Battery
sections.body:
The US Air Force awarded Boeing a $2.82 billion contract for 15 additional KC-46A Pegasus tankers under Lot 13, completing the final production batch under the program's original 2011 fixed-price contract and bringing the total aircraft under contract to 188 for the USAF (and 203 globally), Defense News and Breaking Defense report. While the Air Force plans to procure up to 75 additional KC-46s under a bridge program as its Next-Generation Air Refueling System remains delayed, the original fixed-price structure has cost Boeing more than $7 billion in cumulative charges. Meanwhile, the US Army confirmed that delivery of its first Bell MV-75 Future Long-Range Assault Aircraft prototype for flight testing has been officially delayed due to funding shortfalls.

On the strike side, Lt. Gen. Francisco Lozano, director of hypersonic, directed energy, space and rapid acquisition, confirmed to Breaking Defense that the Army's first Dark Eagle Long-Range Hypersonic Weapon (LRHW) battery is now 'fully fielded' after years of launcher and test delays. By contrast, The War Zone reports that Senate appropriators are moving to scale back funding for a ship-killing variant of the air-launched AGM-183A ARRW hypersonic missile.
sections.whyItMatters: Closing out Boeing's loss-making initial KC-46 contract clears the way for renegotiated pricing on follow-on tankers, while the operational fielding of the first Dark Eagle battery gives the US Army its first land-based hypersonic strike unit.

sections.heading: Japan and India Finalize Pact to Test Japanese Long-Range Missiles and Drones at Indian Ranges
sections.body:
Japan and India are finalizing a defense agreement allowing the Japan Self-Defense Forces (JSDF) to conduct live-fire testing and training with long-range anti-ship missiles and attack drones at Indian military test ranges, according to Defense News. A Japanese defense delegation inspected Indian range facilities in October to verify telemetry and safety parameters after Tokyo concluded that its domestic islands lack sufficient airspace and maritime clearance to test weapons with ranges exceeding 1,000 kilometers.

The bilateral arrangement marks a major operational upgrade in Indo-Japanese defense ties as Tokyo fields upgraded Type 12 surface-to-ship missiles and loitering munitions under its counterstrike doctrine. The move comes as South Korea scrambled F-15K fighters on Wednesday after Russian Tu-160 bombers and fighter escorts approached within seconds of South Korean airspace, prompting local shelter warnings, The War Zone and SCMP report.
sections.whyItMatters: Sharing sovereign missile test ranges moves the India-Japan partnership beyond naval exercises into joint strike weapons development, solving Tokyo's geographic testing bottleneck as Russian and North Korean air and missile activity intensifies.

sections.heading: Israel Expands Defense Budget by $5 Billion to $55 Billion as US Approves $622 Million F-16 Sustainment Sale for Ukraine
sections.body:
Israel's Finance and Defense Ministries approved an additional $5 billion allocation for military spending, lifting the country's total 2026 defense budget to approximately $55 billion, Breaking Defense and Envanter Medya report. The supplemental package — funded through domestic spending cuts and higher deficit borrowing — aims to replenish interceptor stockpiles, sustain prolonged reserve deployments, and finance precision munition procurement.

In Eastern Europe, the US State Department approved a potential $622 million Foreign Military Sale to Ukraine covering F-16 fighter maintenance, sustainment equipment, and technical support, according to The Independent and Anadolu Agency. However, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told The Kyiv Independent that Kyiv has received 'no good news' from Washington regarding accelerated deliveries of Patriot air defense interceptors, even as newly delivered German Rheinmetall Lynx KF41 infantry fighting vehicles begin counter-drone defense missions in Ukraine, The War Zone reports.
sections.whyItMatters: Sustaining high-intensity air defense and strike operations is straining both budgets and interceptor supply chains, forcing Israel into repeated fiscal supplements and leaving Ukraine dependent on European gun-based counter-drone platforms while US Patriot deliveries lag.

sections.heading: China's Air White Whale Unveils 8-Ton W8000 Cargo Drone as RAF Installs Anti-Drone Netting Over UK Airbases
sections.body:
Chinese autonomous aviation firm Air White Whale rolled out its new W8000 heavy uncrewed cargo aircraft, designed to haul an 8-ton payload over regional distances, The War Zone reports. The twin-turboprop autonomous transport significantly expands China's heavy uncrewed logistics fleet, offering dual-use airlift capacity capable of resupplying island outposts and dispersed military airfields without risking flight crews.

At the other end of the uncrewed spectrum, the UK Royal Air Force (RAF) has begun installing physical protective netting and overhead shelters across British airbases to shield parked combat and transport aircraft from small first-person-view (FPV) and quadcopter drone attacks, according to The War Zone. Meanwhile, the US Army successfully tested FireAnt mini uncrewed ground vehicles to autonomously deploy acoustic and RF drone-detection sensors in contested forward zones.
sections.whyItMatters: While China scales uncrewed aviation upward into 8-ton heavy logistics airlift, NATO air forces are being forced to harden homeland airbases with physical netting against low-cost sabotage drones.

sections.heading: Turkey's ASELSAN Validates Laser-Guided TOLUN L on AKINCI UCAV as MKE Develops 127mm Naval Gun for TF-2000
sections.body:
Turkish defense electronics prime ASELSAN successfully completed the first live-fire integration test of its 250-pound class TOLUN L munition — equipped with the KİLİT 310 laser seeker head — launched from a Bayraktar AKINCI UCAV using the SADAK-4T multiple ejector rack over the Saros target range, Anadolu Agency and Daily Sabah report. The laser-guided variant complements the GPS/INS-guided TOLUN by enabling high-precision strikes against moving targets.

In the maritime domain, state munitions manufacturer MKE confirmed it is developing an indigenous 127mm (5-inch) National Naval Gun slated for integration aboard the Turkish Navy's upcoming TF-2000 Air Defense Warfare Destroyer, according to TRT World. Separately, Turkish aircraft engine maker TEI announced a $100 million investment to establish a manufacturing facility in Plovdiv, Bulgaria, marking its first production footprint inside the European Union, while Parliamentary Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Fuat Oktay stated that GE Aerospace F110 engines for the prototype and initial blocks of the KAAN national combat aircraft face no US sanctions delivery blocks.
sections.whyItMatters: Pairing multi-rack laser-guided glide bombs on AKINCI with an indigenous 127mm main gun for the TF-2000 destroyer closes critical foreign subsystem dependencies for Turkey's air and naval strike platforms, while TEI's Bulgarian plant anchors Turkish aero-engine supply inside the EU.

sections.heading: NATO Deploys AWACS to Poland After Airspace Breach as Italy Hits 2.8% Security Spending and Netherlands Targets 40% Industry Growth
sections.body:
NATO decided to deploy an additional Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) aircraft to Poland to reinforce eastern flank radar surveillance following Russia's November 20 drone incursion into Polish airspace, Defense News and RMF24 report. The deployment comes as Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara warned that Russian defense plants have expanded output to approximately 144 ballistic missiles per month — roughly one missile every five hours.

Across Western Europe, Italian officials told Defense News that Rome has reached a combined defense and domestic security outlay equivalent to 2.8% of GDP in 2026 by counting dual-use security expenditures distributed outside the core defense ministry budget. Separately, the Dutch government unveiled a new defense industrial strategy targeting a 40% expansion of domestic defense manufacturing by 2030 to reach 15 billion euros in annual sector revenue, while Norway signed a memorandum of understanding to test Ukraine's combat-proven DELTA digital battlefield management system.
sections.whyItMatters: Russia's output of 144 ballistic missiles per month is driving European NATO members to pair immediate eastern flank AWACS patrols with long-term industrial capacity targets and adoption of Ukrainian digital command software.

bottomLine: The US military passed two major procurement milestones by closing out Boeing's original fixed-price KC-46A contract with a $2.82 billion order and fully fielding its first Dark Eagle hypersonic battery. Across Eurasia, Japan's plan to test long-range missiles at Indian ranges, Turkey's validation of the laser-guided TOLUN L on AKINCI and a 127mm naval gun for the TF-2000 destroyer, and NATO's AWACS deployment to Poland highlight how rapidly states are adapting industrial capacity and base protection to counter massed missile and drone warfare.
sources: Breaking Defense, Defense News, The War Zone, USNI News, Anadolu Agency, Daily Sabah, TRT World, The Independent, The Kyiv Independent, SCMP
